text: What is the structure of a direct proof of a conditional statement P → Q?
choices: Assume P and derive Q through valid inferences
Assume ¬(P → Q) and derive a contradiction
explanation: A direct proof assumes the antecedent P and derives the consequent Q — the →I (implication-introduction) rule. Assuming ¬Q to reach ¬P is proof by contrapositive; assuming the negation to reach ⊥ is proof by contradiction; assuming Q to derive P proves the converse, a different and generally non-equivalent statement.
